content.title: About
content.content: Kale (Brassica oleracea var. sabellica) is a dark, leafy green vegetable belonging to the cabbage family. Unlike head cabbage, its central leaves do not form a compact head. It comes in curly, flat, or dinosaur (Lacinato) leaf varieties and is widely celebrated as a nutrient-dense superfood.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Kale becomes sweeter after experiencing a frost.
It was one of the most common green vegetables in Europe until the end of the Middle Ages.
Lacinato kale is also known as 'dinosaur kale' due to its bumpy texture.
It is exceptionally rich in lutein and zeaxanthin for eye health.
Kale leaves are tough enough to be baked into crispy kale chips.

items.title: Nutrient Powerhouse
items.content: Packed with vitamins A, K, C, and B6, along with manganese and calcium.

items.title: Potent Antioxidants
items.content: Contains quercetin and kaempferol with anti-inflammatory properties.

items.title: Supports Eye Health
items.content: High concentrations of lutein and zeaxanthin protect retina health.

items.title: Cholesterol-Lowering
items.content: Binds bile acids in the digestive system to help reduce cholesterol levels.

items.title: Bone Support
items.content: High in plant-based calcium and vitamin K necessary for bone structure.

items.title: Thyroid Goitrogens
items.content: Contains compounds that can interfere with thyroid hormone synthesis if consumed raw in excessive amounts.

items.title: Oxalates
items.content: Contains moderate oxalates; those prone to kidney stones should monitor intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Massage raw kale leaves with olive oil and lemon juice for tender salads, sauté with garlic, or bake into chips.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Wrap unwashed kale in a damp paper towel and store inside a sealed plastic bag in the refrigerator for up to 5-7 days.
